claims.claim: URINARY ALKALINISATION MAY RELIEVE THE DISCOMFORT OF UTIs, HELP TREAT CERTAIN TYPES OF RENAL STONES, OR BE USED IN SPECIALIST SETTINGS TO TREAT SOME METABOLIC AND RENAL DISORDERS. ⚠️ ALKALINISATION IS NOT POSSIBLE IF CrCl IS BELOW 30 mL/MINUTE
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Urinary alkalinisation and acidification' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/genitourinary-drugs/other-drugs-urinary-tract-disorders/urinary-alkalinisation-acidification, July 2026 release ('Last modified by AMH: July 2026'), read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: SODIUM BICARBONATE WITH SODIUM CITRATE, CITRIC ACID AND TARTARIC ACID: USE 1-2 SACHETS IN A GLASS OF WATER UP TO 4 TIMES DAILY FOR SYMPTOMATIC RELIEF OF UTI. ⚠️ THE SACHET CONTAINS APPROXIMATELY 28 mmol (644 mg) OF SODIUM
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Urinary alkalinisation and acidification' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/genitourinary-drugs/other-drugs-urinary-tract-disorders/urinary-alkalinisation-acidification, July 2026 release ('Last modified by AMH: July 2026'), read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: SODIUM BICARBONATE CAPSULES: USE ALONE AS AN ALKALINISER, eg IN THE TREATMENT OF RENAL TUBULAR ACIDOSIS. DOSE ACCORDING TO RESPONSE -- 1-6 CAPSULES DAILY. Each 840 mg capsule contains 10 mmol (230 mg) sodium
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Urinary alkalinisation and acidification' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/genitourinary-drugs/other-drugs-urinary-tract-disorders/urinary-alkalinisation-acidification, July 2026 release ('Last modified by AMH: July 2026'), read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: POTASSIUM CITRATE: USE 3-6 TABLETS DAILY IN 2 OR 3 DOSES, WITH OR AFTER FOOD, TO PREVENT CALCIUM OR URIC ACID KIDNEY STONES. Each 1.08 g tablet contains 10 mmol (390 mg) potassium. ⚠️ AVOID IN PEOPLE WITH, OR AT RISK OF, HYPERKALAEMIA
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Urinary alkalinisation and acidification' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/genitourinary-drugs/other-drugs-urinary-tract-disorders/urinary-alkalinisation-acidification, July 2026 release ('Last modified by AMH: July 2026'), read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: ⚠️ THE SODIUM-CONTAINING ALKALINISERS MUST BE USED WITH CAUTION OR AVOIDED IN PEOPLE WHO REQUIRE SODIUM RESTRICTION, and the potassium-containing product must be avoided in people with or at risk of hyperkalaemia. ⚠️ THE TWO PRODUCT FAMILIES ARE THEREFORE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Urinary alkalinisation and acidification' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/genitourinary-drugs/other-drugs-urinary-tract-disorders/urinary-alkalinisation-acidification, July 2026 release ('Last modified by AMH: July 2026'), read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: URINARY ACIDIFICATION MAY RARELY BE USED to increase the excretion of LIPID-SOLUBLE BASIC DRUGS, to treat certain types of renal stones, or IN COMBINATION WITH METHENAMINE HIPPURATE. Products used include AMMONIUM CHLORIDE AND ASCORBIC ACID. ⚠️ EVIDENCE FOR EFFICACY IS LIMITED
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Urinary alkalinisation and acidification' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/genitourinary-drugs/other-drugs-urinary-tract-disorders/urinary-alkalinisation-acidification, July 2026 release ('Last modified by AMH: July 2026'), read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: For uric acid stone prevention, target urinary pH 6 to 7 via diet plus citrate salts (potassium citrate preferred) or sodium bicarbonate if citrate unsuitable; citrate salts also for hypocitraturia in calcium stone formers and for cystine stones.
claims.locator: Therapeutic Guidelines (eTG complete), Kidney and Urinary guideline: 'Kidney and ureteric stones in adults' at https://app.tg.org.au/viewTopic?etgAccess=true&guidelinePage=Kidney%20and%20Urinary&topicfile=kidney-overview&guidelinename=auto&sectionId=c_KUG_Kidney-and-ureteric-stones-in-adults_topic_13, accessed 2026-09-24 through the owner's subscription, section 'Measures to prevent uric acid / calcium / cystine kidney and ureteric stones'
